results.title: User A: sign-up through the form, creates a project, a template and a version
User A: moves a project to the trash
User B in the same profile: no projects, templates or trash of A, own 33 starter projects
Quota of B starts at 0 (A's diagrams are not counted)
Projects are stored under a key of each user
Version history (Git panel) of A is not visible to B
results.note: B sees the version history of A (key dslkit.git-commits is shared by all accounts): expected (0, False), got (2, True)

results.title: Settings of A (editor guides) do not change the settings of B
results.note: B inherited the setting of A (key dslkit.settings is shared): expected True, got False

results.title: Theme chosen by A is not applied to B (theme per account)

results.title: Search and filter state of the dashboard is not carried from A to B
results.note: B sees the search text of A in the project search (key dslkit.dashboard): expected '', got 'A-secret'

results.title: A signs in again: projects, template, trash and quota are exactly as left
Separate browser context: no accounts and no data of A, the same email can be registered there
User: five new diagrams a day, the sixth and a re-save after delete are refused, edits of an existing one work
Developer: 7 new diagrams, the quota says no daily limit
Admin: 7 new diagrams, the quota says no daily limit
Switching accounts in one profile keeps each user's quota separate
Projects saved as a guest stay with the guest and do not enter a new account
Sign-out in tab 1 sends tab 2 to sign-in and updates the editor menu; sign-in updates it back
results.note: tab 2 (dashboard) stayed on a private page after sign-out in tab 1: http://localhost:56128/en/app/dashboard.html

results.title: Two tabs save the same project: the last write wins, one record, valid JSON, no errors
A project trashed in tab 1 is not resurrected or duplicated by a save in tab 2
results.note: a project trashed in tab 1 came back or was duplicated by an edit in tab 2: ['Zombie edit']

results.title: Share link: opens for a guest, for another account and in another context; a damaged link does not break the editor
